titleText.es: Los niños son experimentos genéticos. ¡Lo único que hacemos es experimentar de forma responsable!
titleText.en: Kids are genetic experiments.  We're just experimenting responsibly!
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish text and the official English image title make the same joke about treating children as genetic experiments while claiming that the experimentation is responsible; the English text preserves the official two-space sentence break.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bebidas is the feminine plural noun for things people drink.
Azucaradas describes feminine plural things that contain sugar or have had sugar added.
Intentas is the present form of intentar for one familiar person. Follow it directly with an unchanged action verb to say what that person tries to do.

example.en: Are you trying to open the window?

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to cause something in someone; to give someone a condition
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Provocarle combines provocar with attached le. The result or condition is named separately, while le identifies one person affected by it; a later phrase beginning with a can clarify that person.

example.es: El polvo puede provocarle tos a Luis.
example.en: The dust can give Luis a cough.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Diabetes is normally a feminine noun in Spanish: la diabetes.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: we cut off; we discontinue; we cut off (completed past)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cortamos is the nosotros form of cortar in both the present and the completed past. With a service, supply, cable, or connection, cortar can mean stopping or disconnecting it rather than literally slicing it; context shows the time intended.

example.es: Ayer cortamos el servicio durante una hora.
example.en: Yesterday we cut off the service for an hour.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the; English often uses a possessive because le already marks the affected owner
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish can use le for the affected owner and an ordinary article before that person's item or service. English often uses a possessive word instead. El matches a masculine singular item, not the owner's gender.

example.es: Le cancelaron el servicio a Laura.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Insulina is a feminine noun for the hormone and medicine used to control blood sugar.

example.es: La insulina regula el azúcar en la sangre.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A paradigma is a model or general way of understanding and approaching something. Despite its final -a, it is masculine: el paradigma.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: for; links a model or approach to its field
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After words such as modelo, método, or paradigma, de can introduce the activity or field to which that approach belongs. English may use ‘for,’ ‘to,’ or a noun placed before another noun.

example.es: Probamos un nuevo paradigma de enseñanza.
example.en: We tried a new teaching paradigm.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Paternidad can name the state of being a parent or the work and approach involved in raising children.

example.es: El curso trata sobre la paternidad.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that a plan, attempt, or situation goes wrong or turns out badly?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of salir followed by mal.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Salir changes for person and time, while mal stays unchanged: sale mal, salió mal, or puede salir mal. This use describes an outcome, not physical movement out of a place.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: me arreglan el móvil · van a lavarle el coche
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can Spanish identify the person affected through a body part, possession, or other closely connected noun without putting a possessive word before it?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Mark the affected person with me, te, le, nos, or les, then use el, la, los, or las before the closely connected noun.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short person word goes before a changed verb, as in le repararon, or attaches to an unchanged -ar, -er, or -ir form, as in repararle. The article matches the related noun, whether it names a body part, possession, service, or closely associated aspect. Natural English often expresses that relationship with my, your, his, her, our, or their.

example.es: Van a lavarle el coche a Ana.
example.en: They are going to wash Ana's car.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does calling this a ‘Jurassic Park’ parenting approach make the plan darkly comic?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Jurassic Park's engineered dinosaurs were supposed to depend on a supplied nutrient as a containment safeguard; the parent proposes creating a medical dependency and controlling the matching supply.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In the story, the dinosaurs' engineered lysine dependence is meant to keep them under control if they escape. Deliberately causing diabetes and then controlling access to insulin turns that fictional contingency plan into an alarming parenting policy.

applications.explanationEn: Bebidas names the things first, and the neutral description azucaradas follows it.
Azucaradas ends in -as to match the feminine plural noun bebidas.
Intentas changes for one familiar listener, provocar remains in its unchanged -ar form with attached le, and diabetes fills the attempted action's result slot.
Le attaches to the end of the unchanged verb provocar and identifies the person affected.
Context identifies le as the daughter; the condition caused in her is named immediately afterward.

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces a genuinely possible condition, and sale uses the ordinary present form; algo is the condition's subject between them.
Sale is the singular present form of salir for the situation, and mal marks its bad outcome.

applications.exampleEs: LE CORTAMOS EL SUMINISTRO DE INSULINA
applications.explanationEn: Le identifies the daughter as the person affected, while Spanish keeps the masculine article el before the complete item phrase suministro de insulina.
Because le has already identified the daughter, el introduces suministro as her supply while agreeing with that masculine singular noun.

regions.labelEs: USO EL PARADIGMA PARQUE JURÁSICO DE PATERNIDAD.

applications.explanationEn: Parque is the masculine singular noun, and the descriptive word jurásico follows it in the Spanish title.
Jurásico uses masculine singular -o to match parque.
Here de introduces paternidad as the field to which the stated paradigm is being applied.
